tree.note: the user starts with 1, and does 1.5 and 1.6 only when the job needs them. for each element in the design the user goes through 2 - 2.7 for a bought or drawn file, 2.6 for text. then, for each piece, the user shapes it in 3 and sets what the machine will do with each layer in 4, in whatever order the design needs. 5 is needed when a real object or the machine's limit sets a size; this happens before 2 in some videos and after 3 in most. in 6 the canvas is arranged onto mats, and when the preview is wrong the user goes back to 3, 4 or 5. 7 only for a print then cut job. for each mat the user goes through 8 and 9 - five times in z3l5. the task ends at 9.3 on the last mat, or at 9.6 where the software closes the job; the shadow box in j3G1 ends on the canvas without ever reaching 6.

children.label: Assign layers to the machine

questions.say_example: The panel defaults to a scoring wheel. If you don't have one, Edit Tools lets you swap in a scoring stylus.

questions.question: Which pen does the panel want for the drawing step, and in which clamp?
questions.why: The video shows that the 0.4 tip black pen must be pushed into clamp A until it clicks to execute the drawing step properly.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you miss out on learning the tactile feedback of the pen clicking securely into the machine's clamp.
questions.check: What pen type and clamp does the panel instruct for the drawing step?
questions.say_example: The panel wants a <0.4mm black> pen in Clamp A, pushed in until it clicks.

questions.question: What physical steps does the software instruct you to take before clicking Go?
questions.why: The software explicitly prompts you to load the Fine-Point Blade and the mat into the machine to ensure the cut executes correctly.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to physically load the required tools and materials into the machine to complete the project.
questions.check: What physical loading steps does the panel list right before the Go prompt?
questions.say_example: Before you press Go, the panel wants the Fine-Point Blade and the mat loaded.

questions.question: What material setting should you select on the machine's dial?
questions.why: Setting the physical dial to the correct material ensures the machine applies the appropriate blade pressure for the specific project.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the physical control of manually turning the machine's dial to match the exact material they are loading.
questions.verify_form: The agent turned the dial - check it reads Vinyl, or Custom when the software sets the material.
questions.check: Does the panel instruct a specific dial position (a named material, or Custom) for this machine?
questions.say_example: The panel is controlling material digitally, so turn the machine's dial to Custom.

children.label: Load and cut
children.note: for each mat the user goes through 9.1, 9.2 and 9.3 in order - to start the cut the user presses the machine's button, or SEND on Silhouette, or Go in the phone app. in 9.4 the user watches while the machine reads the marks and cuts. in three recordings the user goes through 9.5 before 9.6, and presses Go again if a corner has not cut. 9.6 closes the mat and moves the software to the next one or to Done; for a kiss-cut sheet the user goes through 6 again without printing again. in 25 of the 26 recordings the user goes through 9.7 outside the software after the last mat.

questions.question: What minimum material size does the warning ask for?
questions.why: The screen showed a warning that the material needed to be at least 5 inches long to complete the cut successfully.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user wastes physical material and time if an agent ignores the software's size requirements and attempts a doomed cut.
questions.check: What minimum size does the page's material-size warning state?
questions.say_example: The panel says your material needs to be at least <5 inches> long. Is yours?

questions.question: Do you press the flashing 'Go' button on the machine to start the cut?
questions.why: The software indicates the machine is ready, and pressing the physical flashing button is required to execute the cut job.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent cannot physically interact with the cutting machine to press the button and start the actual cut.
questions.verify_form: The agent pressed Go or waited - check the machine; this is the commit.
questions.check: Does the panel show the machine ready with the Go prompt lit, and has cutting not yet started?
questions.say_example: Ready to cut now on <material>. This runs the blade on the real thing. Press Go, or say wait.

questions.question: Is your cutting machine connected and ready to receive the cut job?
questions.why: Seeing the green 'Ready' status next to your specific machine ensures the hardware is communicating properly before you click the blue 'SEND' button.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you miss the final opportunity to verify the physical machine's connection status before committing your materials to the cut.
questions.check: Does the panel show a green Ready status next to a named machine before Send/Go is enabled?
questions.say_example: Two machines showed up: <Explore 3> and <Joy Xtra>. Which one has your mat loaded?

questions.question: Do you wait for the cutting progress circle to reach 100%?
questions.why: Tracking the on-screen progress percentages ensures you know exactly when the machine has finished cutting the current mat.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to monitor the real-time cutting progress and intervene if the machine stalls.
questions.check: What percentage does the on-screen cutting-progress indicator currently show?
questions.say_example: Tracked cutting progress on <mat 1> - reached 100%

questions.question: Is the machine reading the registration marks?
questions.why: If the optical sensor fails to read the printed black square and corner lines, the machine cannot accurately align the cuts around your printed designs.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to visually verify that the machine's sensor correctly detects the physical registration marks before it begins cutting the material.
questions.check: Does the panel report a registration-mark read failure or scanning error?
questions.say_example: The machine can't read the registration marks on <mat 1>. Try better light, or reprint with a darker border.

questions.question: Did the machine finish the cut?
questions.why: The printed sheet on the cutting mat has been ejected from the machine, indicating the cut job is finished.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to visually inspect the finished product to verify the cut's effectiveness.
questions.check: Does the panel show the job at 100% with a completion, eject or unload prompt?
questions.say_example: Cut finished on <mat 1>. The panel says to unload now.

questions.question: Does the progress shown match the machine having actually started?
questions.why: The software displaying '81% Cutting' before the mat is even loaded indicates a synchronization error or a fabricated demonstration.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to trust the software's progress indicators if the agent cannot detect when the digital status contradicts physical reality.
questions.check: Does the progress indicator show active cutting while the panel still shows the mat as not loaded?
questions.say_example: The panel says <81>% cutting, but it's still asking you to load the mat. That doesn't line up. Worth a look.

questions.question: Was Done clicked so the software is back on the canvas?
questions.why: The screen shows the final steps of the 'Herstellen' process and a green 'Fertig' button to finalize the job.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the final confirmation that the cut job is complete and the control over resetting your workspace.
questions.check: Does the panel show a Done/Finish button, and has it returned to the canvas?
questions.say_example: Closed the job - back on canvas

questions.question: Which color material should you load onto the mat next?
questions.why: The app displays a coral square to indicate the specific color layer that the machine is ready to cut next.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the physical confirmation that the correct color material is loaded to match the software's current cut layer.
questions.check: What color or material does the panel show queued for the next mat?
questions.say_example: Next up is the <coral> layer. Load that material when you're ready.

children.label: Finish the object
children.note: these steps happen outside the software and on camera in 25 of the 26 recordings. the task in TASK.txt ends before them. for every cut the user goes through 9.7.1 and then 9.7.2. the next steps depend on the project: 9.7.3 and 9.7.4 for a decal or a stencil, 9.7.5 to 9.7.7 for iron-on, Infusible Ink and sublimation, 9.7.8 after a stencil is applied. 9.7.9 where pieces are glued, trimmed or fitted with hardware. 9.7.10 is the last step in every recording that shows the project completed.

questions.question: What heat settings and procedure does the guide show for this material?
questions.why: The screen details critical application instructions like 'Medium 25 s' and 'Light pressure' needed to properly adhere the iron-on design to the cotton.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to familiarize yourself with the specific heating times, pressure, and peeling instructions required to successfully finish your physical craft.
questions.check: What temperature, time, and pressure does the heat-settings screen show for the selected material?
questions.say_example: The guide says <Medium, 25 seconds, Light pressure> for this material.
